plan.title: STRING-anchored co-expression modules tracking drug treatment (3v3 liver)
plan.analytical_narrative: The cohort is 3 treated vs 3 control human liver samples with 12000 genes of Salmon-derived gene-level counts — 6 samples total, below the ~15-sample floor at which a co-expression network built from expression correlations alone reflects noise rather than shared regulation (rule R-0140@3faf). The plan therefore does NOT build an expression-only WGCNA network. Instead it takes the rule's sanctioned alternative: modules are communities of the STRING 12.0 prior protein-association network (high-confidence edges, score >= 700) restricted to the expressed, filtered genes, with the DESeq2 variance-stabilized expression used only to weight prior edges and to compute module eigengenes. The pipeline: QC the sample structure on blind vst (T1S1), filter low counts and produce size factors plus the vst matrix (T1S2), build the prior-network modules and their eigengenes (T2S1), test which module eigengenes track the treatment with group-label permutation and BH adjustment (T2S2), and report everything with the n=6 instability stated beside every module (T1S3). Salmon counts carry no statement of length correction, so T1S2 verifies the matrix and rounds fractional values if present before the median-of-ratios size factors.

flags.message: If the cohort holds at most two groups of at most 7 samples, the total is below 15 samples, and a correlation across so few samples is unstable. Do not build a co-expression network from the expression alone on such a cohort, because the modules would reflect the noise of the correlations and not a shared regulation. State the sample count and the reason in the plan. Then either take a prior network, for example the STRING protein-protein associations of the reference store, as the structure and place the genes of interest on it, or stop and ask for a cohort of at least 15 to 20 samples.
